attempts.paper_title: Cell Atlas and Novel Signal Processing Strategy in Primate Insular Cortex
attempts.entry_title: Local connectivity of VENs and PCs in macaque insular cortex (Liu et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's local-circuit finding held in direction but not in its counts. Every VEN connection rate was below the matching pyramidal-cell rate, yet the data gave 26 connections against 31, and none of the four reported rates matched. The files carry no cell types or connection labels, so the counts rest on an annotation table from the paper's code that disagrees with the paper's totals. Lower sodium current, lower phase peak index, larger evoked responses and lower spontaneous event frequency in VENs reproduced on tables or sister dandisets. Soma distances could not be tested because no positions are stored, and the sequencing, morphology and modeling claims were not attempted. The file still needs to be created with this text.
attempts.description: Tests the multi-patch connectivity findings of Fig. 5d-i of Liu, Huang, Shen, Shao, Jing et al. (2026) on dandiset 001751, which holds the paired recordings from 56 slices of six macaques. Cell types and annotated connections come from the paper's code table, linked to the files by name. It counts tested pairs, cells and connections by cell class and looks at the example slice of Fig. 5d-h. Some findings on data in other archives are tested on the paper's code tables, on dandiset 001750 and on MetaboLights MTBLS13927.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Liu et al. (2026), Fig. 5d-i, from dandiset 001751

outcomes.statement: The rows of the paper's metadata_multiPatch.xlsx (cell types, tested pairs and annotated connections) can be linked to the dandiset's files and channels, and they agree with what the files hold.
outcomes.source: Code availability; github.com/RFLiu2021/AIC_proj at commit 44cd8a6, ephysio/data_ephy/rawdata_ephysio/metadata_multiPatch.xlsx
outcomes.notes: The table names 288 files, all in the dandiset. Ten presynaptic blocks name no file; 8 are matched one to one to a file of their slice by the firing channel, and 2 (190315s2 channel 7, 20241014HS2 channel 8, 13 rows, no annotated connection) have no file in the dandiset. The table's presynaptic channel is the channel that fires on the first pulse in 286 of the 288 files it names (99.3%; 281, 97.6%, when a pre-pulse mean below -30 mV is also required); the 8 linked files match by construction, which gives 294 of 296 (289 with the -30 mV rule). In the other 2 it does not overshoot 0 mV (median peaks -21.5 and -8.0 mV). The postsynaptic channel holds a cell in 1,372 of 1,403 pairs (97.8%; 1,391 at -20 mV, 1,304 at -50 mV); 6 pairs of slice 190314s1 name channels 6 and 7, which read 0 mV. The dandiset holds 5 files the table does not list (slice 20240912HS2). Read block by block, the table lists no ordered pair twice, gives 5 cells two types, labels 2 connections with a projection that names another postsynaptic channel (in both, that channel shows the larger deflection, ratio 47.16 against 2.83 and 17.35 against 8.49, on the first sample of the window), and its Nr_Conn disagrees with its annotations in 4 of 53 slices. Annotated connections have a median peak to baseline s.d. ratio of 8.7 in the averaged trace against 2.8 for other pairs, and 11.92 at the pulse against 3.52 in a window 35 ms earlier; 333 of 1,377 pairs not annotated exceed a ratio of 5. Eight Inh connections come from a PC, 6 of 12 Inh have a positive peak, and the Inh postsynaptic cells sit at -67.6 to -78.4 mV (median -69.9), not the -60 mV the Methods give for uIPSPs.
deviations: The criterion was written by the author after the file survey and before any claim's analysis; the presynaptic rule (0 mV within 8 ms in half the sweeps, empty channels within 1 mV of 0 mV excluded) and the -30 mV cell rule are the author's standard choices, and the table's channel numbers are taken as the files' channel numbers.

The table gives the file name once per presynaptic block and 10 blocks name none; 8 are matched one to one to a file of their slice by the firing channel, and the 2 with no file in the dandiset (190315s2 channel 7, 20241014HS2 channel 8, 13 rows, no annotated connection) are left out of the counts and shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: In the example slice of Fig. 5d-h (six simultaneously recorded excitatory neurons), PC cell 2 evokes EPSPs in cell 6, and VEN cell 4 evokes no EPSP in any of the other cells.
outcomes.source: Figure 5d-h
outcomes.quote: f , Traces showing a PC-to-PC connection (from cell 2 to cell 6, bottom block) ... g , Similar to f . Testing of projections from a VEN (cell 4) to other neurons, with no evoked EPSP detected.
outcomes.notes: The table annotates cell 2 to cell 6 (channel 2 to 8 of slice 190315s4) as Ext, Excellent, and none of the five pairs from cell 4 (channel 6); its types for the six cells equal those of Fig5e_plotConnexampleFPs.m. In the averaged traces cell 6's response to cell 2 is +0.162 mV at 8.24 ms, 25.1 times the baseline s.d., the largest of cell 2's targets. From cell 4, cell 5 shows +0.511 mV on the first sample of the window (1.00 ms, ratio 30.6), the time of the presynaptic spike, as a pulse-locked artefact would; cell 2's responses in cells 1 and 3 also peak on that sample (ratios 4.0 and 10.0); the other four responses to cell 4 have ratios of 1.9 to 2.4. The traces describe and do not decide.

outcomes.notes: Blocked by its criterion (the paper prints neither the reference rate nor what comparable allows). The PC-to-PC rate here is 18 of 743, 2.42%.

outcomes.statement: eEPSP amplitudes are higher in VENs than in adjacent PCs, with effects of cell type and stimulation level in an ANOVA.
outcomes.source: Results, VENs respond robustly to deep-layer synaptic input, paragraph 1; Figure 4j
outcomes.quote: whereas the response amplitudes in VENs were significantly higher than those in adjacent PCs (analysis of variance (ANOVA), P = 0.0034 for cell type and P < 0.001 for stimulation level
outcomes.notes: From sumData_StimWM.xlsx (block copied data), 23 VEN-PC pairs at three stimulation levels (0.5, 1 and 2, stated mA). Median VEN amplitude exceeds PC at every level (0.0028 against 0.0010, 0.0086 against 0.0054, 0.0174 against 0.0068, unit not stated); VEN above PC in 54 of 69 pair-levels and 20 of 23 pairs. Cell type effect p = 0.0056 in the ordinary two-way ANOVA (F = 7.93) and p = 0.0065 in the repeated-measures ANOVA with the pair as subject (F = 9.04, df 1 and 22); paper P = 0.0034. Stimulation level p = 0.00018 and p < 0.00001. The first sheet holds the block copied data (stim current, EPSP_amp_PC, EPSP_amp_VEN) and two re-organized blocks labelled by VEN subtype; the copied data block is used.
deviations: The table holds 23 pairs, the paper states 26.
Pairs are read as the blocks of three rows separated by blank rows; the table does not name them.
The Methods' selection of monosynaptic eEPSPs cannot be applied to amplitudes alone; the table's values are assumed to be the selected ones, as the paper's code tables them for Fig. 4j.

outcomes.statement: In Pan-Nav stained sections the AIS of VENs lies farther from the soma than that of PCs, and VENs have a shorter AIS.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 2; Figure 3c
outcomes.quote: showed that the AIS in VENs was, on average, located significantly farther from the soma than in PCs (Fig. 3c ). Additionally, VENs had a shorter AIS than PCs.
outcomes.notes: AIScmp_PCvsVEN_Fig5c.xlsx holds 120 VEN and 500 PC values of AIS distance and length (paper 108 and 430) and no slice or animal per cell, so neither reading of the criterion's two-way ANOVA can run. As a variant that does not decide, the two-sided rank-sum test gives VEN AIS distance median 15.85 against 3.95 um (p = 3.1e-42) and length 24.33 against 29.13 um (p = 2.3e-16), in the paper's direction.

outcomes.quote: The postsynaptic response latencies were similar between VENs and PCs (5.13 ± 0.29 ms for VENs and 5.02 ± 0.30 ms for PCs, two-tailed paired t -test: P = 0.8941)
outcomes.notes: The data the claim names, sumData_StimWM.xlsx, hold amplitudes only, no latencies, and the paper does not say which dandiset holds the raw recordings. Not tested. The claim's data are elsewhere, so the block is other, not data_missing (protocol, author, step 1.4).

outcomes.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 5c
outcomes.quote: whereas the amplitudes were not significantly different between VENs and PCs (Fig. 5c )
outcomes.notes: Same cells as fig5b-psc-frequency. Median amplitude PC against VEN, sEPSC 0.136 and 0.116 (p = 0.1087), sIPSC 0.359 and 0.376 (p = 0.6943), mEPSC 0.073 and 0.066 (p = 0.5737), mIPSC 19.7 and 15.3 pA (p = 0.1399); none below 0.05. outcomes.statement: Somatic Na+ currents in outside-out patches are lower in VENs (n = 14) than in L5 PCs (n = 21).
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 4d
outcomes.quote: outside-out patch-clamp recording showed that the somatic Na + currents evoked in VENs ( n = 14) were significantly lower than those of L5 PCs ( n = 21) (Fig. 4d )
outcomes.notes: 35 files of DANDI:001750 (0.260825.0222, 100 kHz, step at 20 ms), types from the code's metadata_outSideOutSodiumCurrentRec.csv matched by file name (14 VEN, 21 PC). Largest inward current of the step-averaged traces, low-passed at 1 kHz, baseline over the 2 ms before the step, steps up to 0 mV, 0.2 to 3 ms after the step: VEN median -17.3 against PC -31.5 pA, rank-sum p = 0.0010; it agrees with the code's max_Na_current (r = 0.99, median difference 1.28 pA), whose own p is 0.0010 (VEN -14.9, PC -29.3 pA); with steps up to +85 mV, r is 0.77 to 0.94. VENs are lower under all 40 readings run. Low-passed at 500 Hz to 2 kHz, p is 0.0006 to 0.0040 under every window (to 3, 5 or 10 ms) and step range (to 0 or +85 mV). Unfiltered, p is 0.0067 to 0.0956 depending on the window, r with the code 0.40 to 0.90, and 6 of 35 peaks fall later than 3 ms (up to 9.99 ms), where the low-passed peaks fall at 0.59 to 1.42 ms. Question for the paper's authors in findings.
deviations: Assumed. The Methods give the steps (-80 to 0 mV, 25 ms, leak subtracted online, 100 kHz) but neither a filter nor the window in which the peak is taken; unfiltered, the outcome changes between windows ending at 3 ms and at 5 or 10 ms. A 1 kHz low-pass (2nd-order Butterworth, forward and backward, the form of PatchAnaLab's filters; the paper's code applies filter_1000Lowpass to first-AP traces in extFig9ad_plotVENsubtypeAP_Cmp.m, line 35, and Fig4d_plotNaCurrent.m calls no filter, both printed in the notebook) is adopted because the peaks it gives reproduce the code's per-patch max_Na_current (r = 0.99); with it the window does not change the result.

Steps up to 0 mV and the baseline over the 2 ms before the step follow Fig4d_plotNaCurrent.m (nTraces = 17, test pulses from -80 to 0 mV; base over the first 2 ms of a snippet starting 2 ms before the step).

Reading (b), current per patch area from capacitance, cannot run; the files hold no capacitance. The Methods take every patch to be about 5 um2, so (b) divides every patch by the same area and gives the same test as (a).

outcomes.statement: VENs have lower AP phase-plane peak indices than every PC type.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 3e
outcomes.quote: The VENs had lower phase peak indices than any type of PCs (Fig. 3e )
outcomes.notes: From the code's PeakIdx_Fig5e.xlsx; VEN median 0.116 (n = 32) is the lowest of six types (L2/3 IT 0.218 n = 33, IT RORB 0.271 n = 24, L5 IT 0.247 n = 124, L5 ET 0.264 n = 20, L6 PC 0.286 n = 16). Kruskal-Wallis H = 41.80, p = 6.5e-08. Dunn's test with Bonferroni over 15 pairs, VEN against each PC type, p from 3.2e-08 to 0.001. The legend's counts (as Fig. 2d-f) are smaller, VEN 22, L2/3 IT 30, IT RORB 17, L5 IT 119, L5 ET 16, L6 PC 13, so the table holds more cells than the paper analysed.

Bonferroni correction for Dunn's test, from the statistics sheet of the same table (the legend names Dunn's test without a correction).

outcomes.statement: Of 581 metabolites, 228 differ between AIC and V1 and only 108 between AIC and parietal cortex.
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical metabolomics reveals a glycolytic bias of the AIC, paragraph 1; Figure 8a
outcomes.quote: we identified 228 differentially abundant metabolites between the AIC and V1 (Welch's ANOVA test followed by Games–Howell test, P < 0.05) compared with only 108 between the AIC and PrC

findings.statement: The files carry no cell type, no connection label and no soma position for any cell, and the stimulated cell of a file is not named correctly (below), so none of the Fig. 5 counts can be made from the dandiset alone. Types and connections exist only in the paper's code table metadata_multiPatch.xlsx, which links to the files by name.

Every response series states a rate of 1 Hz; the data are sampled at 25 kHz (the stimulus series' rate, the code's 25 kHz, and the 50-sample pulse that is the Methods' 2 ms pulse). The stimulus series gives its rate of 25,000 with the unit millisecond.
The stimulus amplitude is stored as 2 (2.5 or 3 in 14 files) with the unit amperes; the Methods inject 2 nA.

The stimulus series of every file names electrode Elec_8 as the stimulated one, while the cell that fires on the pulse is on channel 8 in only 35 of 301 files; in 286 of the 288 files the code's table names, the firing channel is the table's presynaptic channel.
All 301 files have the session start time 2018-01-01T01:00+08:00, while the slices are named for dates in 2019 and 2024, and every subject has the same age, P4Y/P6Y, and sex M.

The code's table metadata_multiPatch.xlsx disagrees with the paper's counts. It lists 298 cells, 1,416 ordered pairs (1,403 in files of the dandiset) and 26 connections, where the paper reports 377 neurons, 1,292 pairs and 31 connections; PC-to-PC 18 of 743 against 24 of 503, one VEN-to-PC connection (190315s2, channel 4 to 6, Excellent, with a 1 mV response in the data) where the paper reports none, and pair counts per class that differ from the paper's by more than 10% in 6 of 8 classes (all but VEN-to-IN and IN-to-VEN).

The code's table is inconsistent with itself and with the files. Ten of its presynaptic blocks name no NWB file (8 match a file of the dandiset by the firing channel; 190315s2 channel 7 and 20241014HS2 channel 8, 13 rows, match none), it gives 5 cells two types, labels 2 connections with a projection that names another postsynaptic channel (20240912HS5 4 to 1 labelled 4 to 3, 20241105HS16 6 to 3 labelled 8 to 5), and its Nr_Conn disagrees with its annotations in 4 of 53 slices. Six of its pairs name channels that read 0 mV in their file (slice 190314s1, channels 6 and 7). Eight of its Inh connections come from a PC, and 6 of its 12 Inh connections have a positive averaged response.
5 files of the dandiset, all of slice 20240912HS2 (23 to 28 sweeps), are not in the code's table, so it is not known whether the paper counted them.
The Methods average responses over more than 20 sweeps; 119 of 301 files hold more than 20 sweeps (median 20, range 1 to 30).

Question for the paper's authors. The paper and its code give no rule for calling a connection (amplitude, latency, noise or test), so the counts rest on the annotations of metadata_multiPatch.xlsx. Was the connection call made by eye on averaged traces, and with which criteria for Excellent, Good and OK quality? Do the 31 connections of the paper include the table's OK connections, and which of the table's pairs and cells make up the 1,292 pairs and 377 neurons?

sumData_StimWM.xlsx holds 23 VEN-PC pairs for Fig. 4j where the paper states 26, and AIScmp_PCvsVEN_Fig5c.xlsx holds 120 VENs and 500 PCs for Fig. 3c where the paper states 108 and 430; the AIS table has no slice or animal per cell, needed for the two-way ANOVA of the legend.

Question for the paper's authors. For the somatic Na+ currents of Fig. 4d, how was max_Na_current measured: which filter, and in which window after the step? Unfiltered peaks separate VENs from PCs when taken up to 3 ms after the step (p = 0.0074) and not up to 5 or 10 ms (p = 0.077 and 0.067); after a 1 kHz low-pass the peaks match the code's values (r = 0.99) and p = 0.0010 in every window. The attempt adopted the 1 kHz low-pass.

The code's processed tables for claims on other data differ in size from the paper. The Patch-seq mapping results hold 14 VEN-L and 15 VEN-S where the paper reports 10 and 11 mapped to L5 ET and L5/6 CT, and map the 273 excitatory neurons to 17 clusters where the paper states 18; the inhibitory Patch-seq mapping is not saved. PeakIdx_Fig5e.xlsx holds more cells per type than the Fig. 3e legend (VEN 32 against 22).

The paper quantifies 581 metabolites (Fig. 8a), while the MetaboLights deposit MTBLS13927 (revision MTBLS13927_01) holds 558 identified metabolites, the same as the code's Metabolic_data.xlsx; with them the AIC-V1 differential count is 175 to 195 under four readings, against the paper's 228.

The MetaboLights deposit MTBLS13927 and the code's Metabolic_data.xlsx disagree on which of two V1 samples is which: the intensities of V1-4-Q in the deposit are those of V1_4_S in the code's table, and the reverse. The deposit names the first AIC sample A1C-1-Q and stores the run mode (rppos, rpneg, hilicneg) in its charge column.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier read the code table from GitHub, queried the archive's asset metadata and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. It gave its own outcome for each claim; 31 of 35 agree with the record as it was.

disagreements.reason: VEN-to-IN 0/54 holds and VEN-to-VEN has 0 connections. But VEN-to-VEN pairs are 59 (expected 110 +/- 11), VEN-to-PC pairs are 146 (expected 200 +/- 20), and there is one annotated VEN-to-PC connection where the criterion needs 0. That pair (190315s2, 4 to 6, Excellent) shows a clear 1.01 mV averaged response, peak/s.d. 95.8.

VEN is lower in every variant, but p < 0.05 in only 4 of 8 window/step variants the author chose (p = 0.008 to 0.096). Reading (b) cannot run. The code's own max_Na_current gives p = 0.001. Problem 2: the peak windows are the author's own and the result splits on them; the notebook's peak correlates with the code's max_Na_current at only r = 0.40 to 0.90 and the VEN medians differ (-23.7 to -30.6 pA against -14.9 pA), so the measure is not validated against the paper's. Reading (b) per area is a constant rescaling of (a) if every patch is about 5 um2.

AIC vs V1 gives 175 to 195 under all four variants, against 228 +/- 23. AIC vs PrC is within tolerance only for log/ungated (98). Problem 4: the test uses the code's table of 558 metabolites, not the MetaboLights deposit of 581; the 23 missing metabolites could bring AIC vs V1 (195) within tolerance, so not_reproduced rests on an incomplete input.

273 excitatory neurons and 17 types (within 18 +/- 1.8). The 33 or 35 non-excitatory neurons fall within 34 +/- 3.4. The inhibitory-type count (17 of 33) is untestable from the saved tables. Problem 8: the 35 (paper 34 inhibitory) includes 1 VEN and 1 PC_L5; the inhibitory-named neurons number 33.
